docs.text: BagaCAD Draw lines, circles and rectangles, offset edges, extrude and edit dimensions directly in Blender. 0.22 Alpha · Blender 5.0+ Install Drag the BagaCAD extension ZIP from your file browser into Blender, then confirm installation. Keep the ZIP intact; enable BagaCAD if prompted. Disable older development copies first. You can also use Edit > Preferences > Get Extensions > menu > Install from Disk… . Both methods are described in the Blender manual . Start Open the 3D Viewport sidebar with N , then select BagaCAD . Key or gesture Action Click Draw in the panel Draw on the active mesh; create an empty mesh if no mesh is active C / B / O during Draw Circle / rectangle / offset; also available as panel buttons Click Dimensions in the panel Start directly in dimension editing on the active mesh F3 > BagaCAD New Drawing Create an empty mesh and start drawing F3 > BagaCAD Draw Start drawing on the active mesh Click Documentation in the panel Open this manual Click points to draw. Close a flat contour to make a face. The viewport header shows the current action. The Dimensions button needs an active mesh. Draw · Shapes & offsets · Guides & grid · Extrude · Dimensions · Shortcuts & settings Short GIF demonstrations are included in the tool pages. Some recordings use earlier development builds; the written shortcuts describe the current defaults. Scope BagaCAD edits the active mesh. Other objects can hide snap targets but are not themselves snap targets. Hidden mesh elements are ignored. X-Ray and Wireframe allow snapping to revealed geometry. Non-planar contours stay open. Dimensions and their locks are temporary tool data, not a persistent CAD constraint system. This alpha is still in development.

docs.text: Dimensions Click Dimensions in N > BagaCAD , or press D while drawing, then select a vertex or an edge. Near an endpoint, the vertex takes priority. A single selected or active element may be picked automatically. A selected vertex shows its incident edge lengths and useful angles. A selected edge shows its length, nearby parallel distances and angles. Lengths follow the scene units; angles use degrees. Change a value Edit the dimensions around a selected vertex; connected faces follow. Key or gesture Action Click a vertex or edge Select the element to measure and edit Click a value Highlight it in blue and type a replacement Drag a value left / right Decrease / increase it Release the drag Confirm the change Ctrl while dragging Use the configured length or angle increments Shift while dragging Adjust ten times more finely Enter / click during input Confirm typed input Esc / right click during input Cancel the edit Ctrl + A during input Select the whole value Ctrl + V during input Paste a value Backspace during input Delete a character Lengths accept units such as mm , cm , m , ft and in . Angles accept values from −360° to 360°. Typed values do not use drag rounding. Vertex anchoring A selected vertex starts anchored . Click its support icon or press Tab outside input to toggle anchoring. Anchored: the selected vertex stays fixed; its neighbours adapt. Free: only the selected vertex moves; the opposite endpoints remain fixed. Shared faces follow without detaching. With no other length locked, a length edit moves along that edge. With locked lengths, the vertex can change direction while free angles adapt. The solver chooses the nearest position satisfying those lengths. For example, at a three-edge corner, lock two lengths and edit the third if a geometric solution exists. If the locks conflict, the edit is refused and the preview restored. Readable angles The display hides composite angles already described by smaller coplanar sectors and redundant directions. Equal angles in different useful sectors can remain; a cube corner keeps its three independent right angles. Locked and currently edited angles remain visible. Arc sizes follow the visible edges and zoom. Labels sit near their arcs with staggered radii to reduce overlap. This changes the display, not the stored constraints. Edge fixed end and locks Key or gesture Action Tab outside input / click the support icon Switch the fixed endpoint of the selected edge Hover a value Reveal its padlock Click the padlock Lock / unlock that dimension A length edit moves the free endpoint along the edge. A parallel distance edit translates the edge. Angle edits try to slide connected endpoints along neighboring directions, changing the edited length when needed to limit distortion. Locked values are kept while neighboring geometry adjusts. If constraints conflict, cancel or unlock a value. Locks last only while Dimensions is active; leaving the mode clears them. Undo and return Key or gesture Action Ctrl + Z during input or a drag Cancel the current preview Ctrl + Z outside input Undo a validated change Backspace outside input Deselect the element Backspace during a drag Cancel the preview Right click outside input Deselect the element D / Esc outside input Return to drawing

docs.text: Draw Place a start point, then add segments. On a face, hold Ctrl when clicking to draw instead of extruding; keep away from a guide handle. Key or gesture Action Left click Place the start point or confirm the next segment Right click Start a new chain Ctrl + click inside a face Start drawing on the face X / Y / Z Lock the corresponding axis; press again to release Shift + X / Y / Z Lock to YZ / XZ / XY; press again to release Type digits Set the active length or angle value Tab Switch between length and angle input Click / Enter Confirm the segment Backspace Delete a digit; outside input, cancel the unfinished chain Ctrl, held Disable mesh, grid and guide snapping; release to restore snapping Ctrl + Z Undo a validated edit; discard any unfinished guide/grid setup first Esc Clear input, setup or selection; otherwise finish the tool Enter without input or selection Finish the tool Precision Use the coloured axes to align successive segments. A typed length fixes distance while the direction follows the mouse. A typed angle fixes the angle while the length changes. Enter both to fix both. Tab alone selects a field without locking it. Drawing snapping is on by default. Hold Ctrl to disable it; release Ctrl to restore it. Axis/plane locks and typed values still apply while Ctrl is held. Snap targets include vertices, midpoints, edges, faces, construction guides, temporary reference points and grid nodes ( Guides & grid ). With a fixed length, any snap target can choose the direction; the segment keeps its entered length. Displayed measurements follow the scene units. Drawing input uses Blender units; angles use degrees. In empty space without a snap, grid plane or explicit constraint, the first point uses a view-parallel plane through the 3D cursor. Each following segment uses a view-parallel plane through its starting point instead. For circles, rectangles and parallel edges, see Shapes & offsets . Faces Close the contour to create a face. Close a flat contour to fill it. Draw between face borders to cut a face. Crossings split edges; overlapping segments merge. To fill a missing flat region, retrace one of its border edges. Existing coplanar faces are not covered. A diagonal across an empty square can fill both sides. Erase and extend edges Key or gesture Action Hold Shift + right mouse, then sweep Erase visible edges under the cursor Release right mouse or Shift End the stroke; one undo step for the whole sweep Esc / Ctrl + Z during the stroke Cancel the sweep and restore the mesh Hold Alt over an edge Preview extension from the endpoint nearest the cursor Alt + left click on the preview Extend to the first real vertex, edge or face target Release Alt Hide the extension preview Erasing B–C in A–B–C–D keeps A–B and C–D. A divider between coplanar faces is dissolved while preserving the surface. Erasing a boundary or an edge between non-coplanar faces also removes its attached faces. Extension joins the target in 3D; a screen-only crossing is not enough. Inside a face plane it targets real boundaries; a transverse arrival into a face makes a local cut. Without a visible target, clicking does nothing. Alt priority: a hovered guide moves first; otherwise an edge can extend, while a face interior keeps coplanar extrusion. In Rectangle, Alt centres the shape. Navigation Key or gesture Action Middle mouse / Shift + middle mouse / wheel Orbit / pan / zoom with the default Blender keymap Numpad during a segment Enter numbers Numpad before the first point Use Blender view shortcuts BagaCAD shortcuts can be changed in the preferences ; navigation uses Blender's keymap.

docs.text: Extrude Hover inside a face with no segment in progress. A light overlay marks the extrusion target. Start the extrusion, move the mouse, then confirm. The face moves along its normal. Key or gesture Action Click a highlighted face Start an extrusion preview Move the mouse Adjust the extrusion distance Type a distance Set an exact distance in Blender units Minus Change the direction of the typed distance Backspace Correct typed distance; without input, cancel the preview Click / Enter during the preview Confirm the extrusion Esc / right click / Ctrl + Z during the preview Cancel it and restore the original mesh Ctrl + Z after confirmation Undo the whole extrusion in one step Undo affects the latest validated edit. Cancelling a preview leaves earlier edits in the local history; press Ctrl + Z again to undo the previous edit. An empty history does nothing. After leaving BagaCAD, Blender handles undo. Extrude the new face into a volume. Several faces Key or gesture Action Shift + click Add / remove a face from the selection Plain click on a selected face Extrude the selection Enter with a selection Extrude along the last selected face's normal Alt + click Replace the selection with connected coplanar faces and extrude them Esc / right click before extrusion Clear the selection For non-coplanar selected faces, the group moves in one common direction: the normal of the last selected face. Coplanar selection spreads only through shared edges, not corner contacts or detached faces. Snapping Height snapping is off by default and is active only while Ctrl is held. Key or gesture Action Hold Ctrl and aim at a vertex, midpoint, edge or face Place the extruded face plane through that snap point Hold Ctrl during extrusion Enable height snapping; release for free movement Orbit / pan / zoom Change the view while keeping the preview active The face still moves only along its extrusion direction. A typed distance takes priority over snapping. Result Push a face inward to remove material from the same mesh. Outward extrusion can fuse with volumes in the same mesh. Inward extrusion can make a pocket or a through-hole. The exact boolean calculation happens when you confirm and remains one undo step. An isolated surface keeps a bottom and becomes a volume. Other objects remain separate.

docs.text: Guides & grid BagaCAD has three drawing references: construction guides , temporary reference points and the construction grid . None of them is mesh geometry, none is rendered, and none is saved in the scene. They add snap targets on top of the mesh snaps. Guide or temporary point? Construction guide Temporary reference point Use Lasting alignment for several segments Quick alignment for the segment in progress Created by Hovering 2 s, or A + two vertices Hovering 0.15 s on a vertex or intersection Form XYZ frame (three axes) or infinite line A point offering XYZ projections and the directions of its edges Display Always drawn Hidden; a dotted link appears only while you follow it Lifetime Until R / Shift + R or the end of the tool Two at most; cleared after each confirmed segment, shape or extrusion Editable Move with Alt , rotate an XYZ frame with Shift No A short hover acquires a temporary point; keep hovering and a guide is created where supported. A small bar under the cursor fills during the guide delay. All four delays are editable in preferences . Construction guides A guide is a fixed reference you build on purpose. An XYZ guide has one origin and three perpendicular axes. An edge guide extends an edge infinitely in both directions. Key or gesture Action Hover a vertex or edge midpoint for 2 s Add an XYZ guide Hover an edge, away from its midpoint and ends, for 2 s Add an edge guide A on a vertex, then click another vertex Add a guide through both vertices Hold Alt over a guide, then move Move the guide; release Alt to confirm Hold Shift over an XYZ axis, then aim Rotate the XYZ guide around its origin; release Shift to confirm X / Y / Z while rotating Lock rotation to that local axis; press again to unlock Esc / right click / Backspace during a move or rotation Cancel it R Remove the last guide Shift + R Remove all guides and temporary points; the grid is kept Guides are not created while typing a value or navigating the view. They stay available between segments, in shapes and offsets, and after switching to Dimensions and back. Moving an XYZ guide moves its three axes together; an edge guide keeps its direction. Snapping is active during the move. Over a guide, Alt moves it; elsewhere Alt keeps its usual role (edge extension, coplanar faces). During a rotation, X / Y / Z refer to the guide's own axes at the start of the gesture. The origin and the locked axis stay fixed. If the grabbed axis is the rotation axis, the next axis supplies the aiming direction. Guide intersections must meet in 3D; a crossing visible only on screen is not a snap. Use an edge extension as a guide for a new contour. This clip uses an earlier development build; use the shortcuts listed above. Temporary reference points A temporary point remembers a position for the segment in progress. It creates nothing and cannot be edited. Key or gesture Action Hover a vertex for 0.15 s, then move away Remember it; its XYZ projections and edge directions become snaps Hover a guide/guide or guide/edge intersection for 0.15 s Remember that intersection Acquire a third point Replace the oldest one Confirm a segment, shape or extrusion Clear the temporary points Right click / Backspace (no input) / Ctrl + Z / Shift + R / D Clear the temporary points Two temporary points work together: their projections can cross each other or cross a guide. Following one projection can also snap where it meets a plane through the other point (XY, YZ, XZ or one of its faces). These planes are not drawn; a dotted link shows which point supplies the snap. Construction grid Key or gesture Action G Show / hide the grid; on first use, create XY at the 3D cursor Shift + G Place or reorient: click the origin, then the X direction G while choosing the direction Toggle using the measured length as cell size Hold Ctrl on the direction click Use the measured length as cell size Ctrl + G Set cell size: measure a segment, or type a value and press Enter Alt + G Place and align the grid on the hovered face Shift + X / Y / Z, no segment in progress Orient a world grid to YZ / XZ / XY Esc / right click during setup Cancel and restore the previous grid The grid snaps to line intersections only. Default step: 0.1 Blender unit. Hiding and showing it keeps its origin, orientation and size for the tool session. R and Shift + R do not affect it. Holding Ctrl while drawing disables snapping to guides, temporary points and grid nodes; the grid stays the drawing plane. Grid setup and guide editing keep their own point picking.

docs.text: Shapes & offsets Use C , B or O during Draw, or the matching button in N > BagaCAD . Press the active tool key again to return to lines. Backspace deletes a digit, or without input resets the placed points. Esc / right click cancels the current shape and returns to Draw. Each confirmed shape is one undo step. Circles and arcs Key or gesture Action C, then two clicks Circle: centre, then radius Type a radius after placing the centre Set an exact radius; click / Enter to confirm Tab Switch centre-radius / three-point method; restart the current shape Three clicks in three-point mode Create a full circle through the three points V Switch full circle / open arc, keeping placed points Wheel after the first click Change segment count without zooming For a centre-based arc, click the centre , start/radius , then end ; the arc runs counterclockwise in its drawing plane. For a three-point arc, it runs from the first point to the third through the second. The radius and edge count appear on the preview. The initial resolution is 48 segments , configurable in preferences; the wheel allows 3–256 during drawing. Before the first click, the wheel still zooms. Arcs remain open lines. Rectangles and squares Key or gesture Action B, then two clicks First corner, then opposite corner Hold Shift Constrain to a square Hold Alt First point becomes the centre; aim at a corner Hold Shift + Alt Centred square Type a size, then Tab Enter width, then height; Tab switches the active side Both side lengths appear on the preview. The active value is highlighted beside its side; the first digit after Tab replaces the previous value. For centred shapes, width and height are the total dimensions . Drawing plane and references Before each new circle or rectangle, hover the target face. Its plane is detected before the first click, including from an incident face when snapping to an edge or vertex. Without a face, the tool uses the active grid, then guides or the view. The plane stays fixed after the first click and is detected again for the next shape. The soft grid around the cursor shows this plane; it is an indicator, not an extra snap grid. X / Y / Z after the first point orients the shape plane to YZ / XZ / XY in the current reference frame. A three-point circle uses the actual 3D snapped points to determine its plane. Construction guides and temporary reference points remain available while drawing shapes and offsets. A creates a two-point guide; G and grid setup commands stay available. Hold Ctrl to suspend placement snapping. The snap marker stays on the target even when the shape needs a projection onto its plane. Offset edges Press O , click an edge, move to the desired side, then click to confirm. Type a distance for an exact offset; the mouse chooses the side. For several edges: O → hold Shift → click the edges → release Shift → move/type → click . Each click adds only the targeted edge, shown in orange. Releasing Shift groups the selection into chains and starts the preview from the last selected edge. Independent chains share the distance and one undo step. Source edges remain in place. Chains must be planar; corners use miter joins and self-crossing offsets are rejected. Offsets work on existing faces or loose edges. Filled faces or lines only Closed shapes create faces by default. Hold F to invert filling while placing a circle, rectangle or offset. The preference Shapes: Create Faces by Default reverses this default. With filling enabled, an offset also creates the connecting strip. With filling disabled, it creates only parallel lines. On an existing face, the new lines still cut the surface: disabling fill does not remove existing material. Shared edges and intersections merge into the active mesh.
docs.title: Shapes & offsets

The initial resolution is 48 segments , configurable in preferences; the wheel allows 3–256 during drawing. Before the first click, the wheel still zooms. Arcs remain open lines.

docs.text: Key or gesture Action B, then two clicks First corner, then opposite corner Hold Shift Constrain to a square Hold Alt First point becomes the centre; aim at a corner Hold Shift + Alt Centred square Type a size, then Tab Enter width, then height; Tab switches the active side Both side lengths appear on the preview. The active value is highlighted beside its side; the first digit after Tab replaces the previous value. For centred shapes, width and height are the total dimensions .
docs.title: Rectangles and squares

docs.text: Before each new circle or rectangle, hover the target face. Its plane is detected before the first click, including from an incident face when snapping to an edge or vertex. Without a face, the tool uses the active grid, then guides or the view. The plane stays fixed after the first click and is detected again for the next shape. The soft grid around the cursor shows this plane; it is an indicator, not an extra snap grid. X / Y / Z after the first point orients the shape plane to YZ / XZ / XY in the current reference frame. A three-point circle uses the actual 3D snapped points to determine its plane. Construction guides and temporary reference points remain available while drawing shapes and offsets. A creates a two-point guide; G and grid setup commands stay available. Hold Ctrl to suspend placement snapping. The snap marker stays on the target even when the shape needs a projection onto its plane.
docs.title: Drawing plane and references

docs.text: Press O , click an edge, move to the desired side, then click to confirm. Type a distance for an exact offset; the mouse chooses the side. For several edges: O → hold Shift → click the edges → release Shift → move/type → click . Each click adds only the targeted edge, shown in orange. Releasing Shift groups the selection into chains and starts the preview from the last selected edge. Independent chains share the distance and one undo step. Source edges remain in place. Chains must be planar; corners use miter joins and self-crossing offsets are rejected. Offsets work on existing faces or loose edges.
docs.title: Offset edges

docs.text: Closed shapes create faces by default. Hold F to invert filling while placing a circle, rectangle or offset. The preference Shapes: Create Faces by Default reverses this default. With filling enabled, an offset also creates the connecting strip. With filling disabled, it creates only parallel lines. On an existing face, the new lines still cut the surface: disabling fill does not remove existing material. Shared edges and intersections merge into the active mesh.
docs.title: Filled faces or lines only
